source.title: Bridging Lottery Ticket and Grokking: Understanding Grokking from Inner Structure of Networks
source.authors: Gouki Minegishi; Yusuke Iwasawa; Yutaka Matsuo

record.file_problem: none; full paper text supplied, including appendices
record.tranche_reason: The study examines delayed generalization (grokking) on algorithmic tasks and MNIST, but does not test any listed claim version about random-label capacity, width, image CNN-versus-fully-connected performance, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own grokking and network-structure results. These concern a different setting from the claim versions, so rows are recorded with versions ["none"]. Prior-work claims are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study tests explanations of delayed generalization and compares pruning methods. It does not test any of V1–V8. Memorizing natural training examples is not fitting random labels; pruning weights is not varying width or removing memorized examples; graph and Fourier metrics are not magnitude-aware sharpness. The discussion of convolutional locality cites prior work without testing V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that grokked tickets reduce delayed generalization, that matching initial norms or sparsity alone does not explain this reduction, and that beneficial subnetwork discovery is central. They also report improved generalization through mask optimization without weight updates. Their causal interpretation is stronger than the structural correlations alone establish.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments study grokking on modular arithmetic, polynomial regression, sparse parity, and MNIST, using lottery-ticket extraction, pruning, and structural measurements; they do not implement the claim versions' tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning rate and ticket-extraction epoch change the reported generalization behavior; the text also reports task and architecture variation across grokking experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokked tickets shorten delayed generalization, with effects depending on extraction time and pruning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subnetworks selected after generalization and reset to their original initial weights can shorten subsequent grokking delays in the tested tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Matching initial norms or sparsity does not reproduce the ticket's faster generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial weight norm and sparsity alone do not explain the grokked-ticket timing advantage in the tested setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Structural changes, periodic weight representations and graph-property changes accompany improvements in held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural and representation metrics track aspects of the grokking transition in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Edge-popup raises held-out accuracy to 0.92 ± 0.06 by epoch 2000 without weight updates; combining it with weight decay improves early accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing a pruning mask can improve generalization from a memorizing solution while keeping underlying weight values fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: A selected grokked ticket with pruning rate 0.81 reaches perfect held-out accuracy without weight decay during retraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay during retraining can be unnecessary after a suitable subnetwork has been discovered in the tested setup.

record.problems: The experiments focus mainly on simple algorithmic tasks; some findings are qualitative descriptions of figures, and Table 1 does not state the task or model. The paper reports three seeds for some experiments but does not provide uncertainty for many figure-described results.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error trends as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of learned locality.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, excessive dropout and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern findings outside the listed versions, so their version-relative states are cannot_determine. This does not dispute the reported grokking effects. The record incorrectly says MNIST findings are represented in rows: none explicitly records Appendix B's MNIST experiment. That omission does not require a missing entry because it bears on no listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its test-error trend.
CNN versus fully connected image-classifier comparisons and the role of locality.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons under tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout comparisons, including training-set-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: Base model
rows.operation_detail: Dense MLP trained on modular addition; compared with a grokked ticket.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy over training; delayed-generalization timing
rows.value: The text says test accuracy improves later than training accuracy; grokked tickets reduce the delay.
rows.uncertainty: Three seeds are reported for Figure 2 experiments; no interval stated here.
rows.note: This is delayed generalization on modular arithmetic, not the natural-label/random-label comparison in V1.
rows.check: Delayed generalization does not measure any listed version. The dense base model has pruning rate 0; the default 0.6 applies to the ticket comparator.

rows.subject: Grokked tickets
rows.stage_stated: ticket extracted at or after the generalizing solution, then trained
rows.operation_detail: Train a magnitude-pruned ticket extracted from a generalized solution.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy over training; delayed-generalization timing
rows.baseline: Base model test accuracy improves later than training accuracy.
rows.value: The text says test accuracy improves at nearly the same time as the base model's training accuracy; delayed generalization is significantly reduced.
rows.uncertainty: Three seeds are reported for Figure 2 experiments; no interval stated here.
rows.note: The intervention is a grokked ticket; the task is algorithmic.
rows.check: A pruning-method result outside V1–V8. Clarify that the extracted mask is applied to the original initial weights before retraining.

rows.subject: Grokked tickets
rows.operation_detail: Vary pruning rate and measure the grokking timing ratio.
rows.baseline: At pruning rate 0.0 (dense network), τgrok is 245.674.
rows.value: τgrok reaches its minimum at pruning rate 0.7; reported values include 5.446 at 0.5, 5.099 at 0.6, 3.629 at 0.7, and 4.266 at 0.8.
rows.note: The text reports the minimum and selected displayed values; other plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Pruning-rate effects on grokking timing do not test V2's width trend beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: Lottery tickets acquired at different epochs
rows.stage_stated: ticket acquired at the stated pruning epoch
rows.operation_detail: Compare generalization after extracting tickets at different training epochs.
rows.baseline: Base model test accuracy; exact numeric value not stated.
rows.value: Tickets obtained before 25k epochs do not fully generalize and correspond to the base model's test accuracy; tickets obtained after 25k epochs get perfect generalization and reduce the delay.
rows.note: The text gives qualitative results and epoch boundary.
rows.check: Ticket-extraction timing is outside V1–V8. The qualitative result agrees with Section 3.2.

rows.subject: Grokked tickets
rows.operation_detail: Vary pruning rate for grokked tickets.
rows.measure: Test accuracy and speed of generalization
rows.value: Most tested rates (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7) accelerate generalization; a rate that is too large (e.g., 0.9) cannot generalize, while a rate that is too small (e.g., 0.3) does not generalize quickly enough.
rows.note: The text's explanation calls 0.3 both among rates that accelerate generalization and too small to generalize quickly; preserve that qualification.
rows.check: Pruning-method performance is outside V1–V8. Acceleration at 0.3 and insufficiently rapid generalization at 0.3 are compatible qualifications.

rows.size_stated: dense model; exact size not stated
rows.stage_stated: initial weights scaled to match grokked-ticket L1 norm
rows.operation_detail: Train a dense model whose initial L1 norm matches the grokked ticket.
rows.baseline: Grokked ticket reaches generalization much faster.
rows.value: The controlled dense model does not reach generalization as fast as the grokked ticket.
rows.uncertainty: Three seeds are reported in Appendix C; no interval stated here.
rows.note: This tests whether matching initial norm alone explains reduced delay.
rows.check: Matching initial L1 norm tests an explanation of grokking timing, not any listed version.

rows.subject: Base model and grokked ticket
rows.operation_detail: Measure Jaccard distance between magnitude-pruned masks at checkpoints and compare with test-accuracy change.
rows.value: During significant test-accuracy changes (16k–20k), maximum mask change corresponds to the change in test accuracy.
rows.note: This measures structural change aligned with accuracy change, not the train-test generalization gap.
rows.check: Figure 7 measures checkpoint-mask changes during dense-model training, not a base-model versus retrained-ticket comparison. Jaccard distance is outside V7.

rows.subject: Base model and grokked ticket
rows.operation_detail: Measure Fourier entropy of neuron weights during modular-addition training.
rows.baseline: Base model Fourier entropy; exact numeric value not stated.
rows.value: The grokked ticket has periodic structure at an early stage (2k epochs) and exhibits a rapid decrease in Fourier entropy; it converges to smaller Fourier entropy faster than the base model.
rows.note: A measured property of grokking, but not the magnitude-aware sharpness or gap ranking in V7.
rows.check: Fourier entropy measures periodic weight structure, not the perturbation tolerance or generalization-gap ranking specified by V7.

rows.subject: Base model
rows.operation_detail: Measure average path length and clustering coefficient as training proceeds.

conditions.value: entire network viewed as relational graph

rows.measure: Average path length and clustering coefficient alongside train/test accuracy
rows.value: Average path length increases alongside test accuracy then converges to a moderate range; clustering coefficient decreases as test accuracy improves, then settles at an intermediate value.
rows.note: The paper describes trends in graph measures, not a measured train-test gap.
rows.check: Graph connectivity trends do not measure any listed version, including V3's image-locality comparison.

rows.subject: WD
rows.operation_detail: Continue training from θmem with weight decay and weight updates.
rows.note: Table 1's setup describes optimization from memorized solutions; task and model are not stated in the table.
rows.check: A weight-decay comparator outside V1–V8. Table 1 labels accuracy as percent but reports fractions: 0.53 corresponds to 53%. The WD trajectory also includes 0.95, 1.00 and 1.00 at epochs 1000, 1400 and 2000.

rows.subject: EP w/o WD
rows.stage_stated: optimization starting from memorized solution; no weight updates
rows.operation_detail: Optimize edge-popup scores without weight updates or weight decay, changing the selected subnetwork by pruning.
rows.note: The authors state that pruning alone improves generalization; the table reports four epoch-specific values.
rows.check: Pruning weights without updating their values does not test V8's removal of training examples. Accuracy values are fractions despite the table's percent heading: 0.92 means 92%.

rows.subject: EP w/ WD
rows.stage_stated: optimization starting from memorized solution; edge-popup and weight decay with weight updates
rows.operation_detail: Combine edge-popup with weight decay and weight updates.
rows.note: The paper says this combination gives the fastest improvement; values do not exceed WD at every listed epoch.
rows.check: A pruning-plus-weight-decay method result outside V1–V8. Values are fractional accuracies; its early advantage over WD does not persist at every reported epoch.

rows.subject: EP w/o WD
rows.stage_stated: optimization starting from memorized solution; no weight updates
rows.operation_detail: Measure graph-property metrics during edge-popup optimization without weight decay.
rows.measure: Weighted spectral gap; spectral gap; Ramanujan gap; average path length; clustering coefficient
rows.note: These structural metrics are measured during pruning; they do not measure the gap specified by the claim versions.
rows.check: These are graph metrics during pruning, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the train–test error gap.

rows.subject: Grokked ticket with critical pruning ratio
rows.stage_stated: ticket extracted after generalization; trained without weight decay
rows.operation_detail: Train the grokked ticket without weight decay at the critical pruning rate.

conditions.value: not stated in Appendix H figure text

rows.baseline: Base model; exact numeric value not stated.
rows.value: The text says test accuracy reaches perfect generalization without weight decay.
rows.note: Appendix H reports the grokked ticket can generalize without weight decay after the structure is discovered.
rows.check: Generalization without weight decay after selecting a ticket does not test V6's dropout intervention or V1's random-label comparison.
